gates.detail: absolute-without-relative: position:absolute (.hero__leak) with no relative anchor found. False positive — the linter only reads the given HTML file and does not follow the linked external styles.css, where .hero (the actual anchor) is declared position:relative. Left as-is rather than gamed with a redundant inline style; documented here per the linter's own 'heuristic — may false-positive' disclaimer.

gates.note: 0 static findings. Not a conformance claim — rendered/behavioural criteria and alt-text quality need a browser or a human, per accessibility.md's two-tier model.

gates.detail: All 8 warnings are container-nesting-depth (Layout axis) — wrapper chains 3-5 levels deep under section > region > sub-region markup (hero actions, terminal body, feature media/copy columns, gate card body/actions, install command panel). Each chain carries real structural payload (grid/flex layout roles, BEM component boundaries) rather than decorative div-soup; accepted as warning-only per the linter's own severity (never blocks the gate) and not raised by Codex's independent review either.

gates.reason: No compiled design system / token registry exists for this output directory — first generation, per taste-rubric.md's Consistency axis ('not yet scorable' for a first generation in an empty project').

findings_addressed.finding: Hero terminal only fades in four predetermined rows — no real queued→running→passed transition; the main proof device reads as cosmetic.
findings_addressed.how: Rebuilt the stage icon as three stacked, crossfading frames (queued dot -> spinning running icon -> final check/pending-dot) per row, sequenced with CSS animation-delay so build finishes, then test starts, then the gate settles into an amber pulsing 'awaiting review' state, purely in CSS (animation-fill-mode both, so it degrades to the correct final frame under the existing reduced-motion override with no JS dependency). Accessible status text (build/test/gate/deploy labels) was left un-animated and always states the true final value, so assistive tech never hears an intermediate/misleading state.

findings_addressed.finding: Nav 'Docs' link and hero's 'View an example pipeline' both pointed at #define — a misleading duplicate CTA, not real documentation access.
findings_addressed.how: Removed the duplicate 'Docs' pill. Nav CTA is now 'Install the CLI' -> #install (mirrors the hero's real primary action instead of a second link to the same anchor); 'View an example pipeline' remains the sole path to the YAML example.

findings_addressed.finding: --fg-2 (#6d7480) measured ~3.6-4.2:1 against the surfaces it's used on (terminal chrome, statuses, meta, footer) — below the 4.5:1 AA floor for normal text.
findings_addressed.how: Brightened --fg-2 to #878e98, verified >=4.5:1 against bg-2 (#1a1c21, the lightest/hardest surface it sits on) by the same relative-luminance math Codex used. All consumers (terminal title, queued/idle status text, gate meta, footer note, code panel bar) inherit the token, so the fix is systemic, not per-instance.

findings_addressed.finding: Approval card presents disabled buttons then immediately disclaims them as a static example — no identity, timestamp, review context, or downstream reaction. Reads as an unfinished component demo.
findings_addressed.how: Added a requester (@priya, 4 minutes ago), a named required reviewer (@jordan, 1 of 1), and an explicit downstream consequence ('deploy starts immediately' on approval) as a definition list, plus a small 'gate:approval — pending' frame bar so the card reads as a captured product screenshot rather than a bare disabled-button mockup.

findings_addressed.finding: Mobile nav hid Pipeline/Approvals but kept a separate, redundant 'Install'/'Docs' pill — arbitrary, not a deliberate mobile hierarchy.
findings_addressed.how: Now a deliberate two-state nav: full link list + CTA on desktop, link list hidden entirely under 640px leaving only the wordmark and the single 'Install the CLI' CTA — a named, common mobile pattern rather than a partial arbitrary hide.

findings_addressed.finding: Gate and install bands use large symmetric padding around small centered content, producing several hundred px of inert dark space at desktop.
findings_addressed.how: Reduced vertical section padding (--sp-7 -> --sp-6) on both bands, widened the gate card (34rem -> 38rem) and gave it real content depth (see above), and added a 3-item checklist under the install command panel so the section carries actual content instead of a lonely centered block.

findings_addressed.finding: All three product visuals (hero terminal, YAML code panel, status list) are variations of the same bordered dark rectangle with mono text — reads as generic/reskinned.
findings_addressed.how: Replaced the 'watch it happen' section's bordered stage-list panel with a horizontal step-rail (connected dots + labels, no bordered rectangle) that restructures to a vertical rail on narrow widths — a genuinely different composition from the terminal and code panel, not a recolor of the same component. The gate card's redesign (above) also moves it away from the mono-text-rectangle pattern toward a labelled definition list.

findings_addressed.finding: The mobile `.stage:nth-child(n+5)` rule can never fire (only 4 rows exist) — dead CSS claiming a mobile treatment that doesn't exist.
findings_addressed.how: Removed the dead rule. Added a real mobile transform instead: under 420px the stage row wraps so the status text drops to its own line under the name, rather than a no-op selector.

findings_addressed.finding:
Forced `
` after 'cadence,' hard-codes the desktop line break and can wrap awkwardly on narrow widths.
findings_addressed.how:
Removed the manual `

findings_addressed.finding: Clipboard copy has no rejection handling — silent no-op on failure.
findings_addressed.how: Added a `.catch()` path and a no-Clipboard-API fallback: both select the command text via the Selection/Range API and flash the button to a distinct 'Select → ⌘C' state with an aria-label update, instead of doing nothing.

imagery.reasoning: The creative direction (generation-contract.json) builds its entire visual language from UI-chrome devices — a simulated terminal, a syntax-highlighted code panel, a step-rail, and a gate card — which are the product's actual interface, not decorative photography or illustration. No point in the section architecture calls for a photographic/illustrative asset; adding one would be imagery for quota's sake, which generation-craft-defaults.md explicitly forbids ('do not generate... add imagery merely to satisfy a quota').

iconography.rule: generation-craft-defaults.md's asset policy calls for the official Phosphor icon package in greenfield work.
iconography.reason: This output is a single static HTML file with no build/package step available, so Phosphor's npm package cannot be vendored in.
iconography.resolution: Hand-authored inline SVG line icons (check, dot, spinner, arrow-right, terminal, shield, copy) — one family, one stroke weight (1.75px), sized on a 16/20/24px ramp via a shared <symbol> sprite — functioning as a deliberate, declared offline substitution for Phosphor.

blinding.result: index.html, styles.css, and script.js contain no comment, meta tag, class name, or copy referencing any model, vendor, tool, generator, 'DESIGN:OS', or 'AI'. Sibling records (this file, design-brief.json, generation-contract.json, critique-codex.md) are not shown to the judge.

offline_rendering.result: No CDN, no remote fonts, no hotlinked images. Type uses the system font stack only. All icons are inline SVG. Verified renders correctly from a local static file server (equivalent to file://) with 0 console errors.
